title: Synthion POC scoping - open models
redwood_attendees: Liam O'Neill (Solutions Engineer - on for benchmarks)
summary: POC scoping to pick a shortlist of open models for a customer-facing multilingual support summarization and classification workload. Covered success criteria (latency, quality, hallucination thresholds), workload sizing, benchmark plan, and timeline for a 4-week pilot. Discussed tradeoffs between Mistral/Falcon/Llama variants and quantization/latency strategies, and security requirements for data residency and SOC2.
topics: Success criteria: latency, quality, hallucination rate, cost per 1M tokens
Workload sizing: concurrent sessions, average turn length, per-month tokens
Benchmark plan: representative prompt sets, multilingual evaluation, automated scoring
Model shortlist: Llama 3 7B/13B, Mistral-Instruct, Falcon 40B, OpenLLaMA variants
Runtime tradeoffs: int8/4-bit quant, KV cache, batching, Dedicated vs Hosted
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro — I'm Jordan, AE, with Priya and Liam from the tech side. how's everyone?
[00:08] Carlos (Synthion): Hey, good thanks, Carlos here. excited to get this scoped.
[00:12] Maya (Synthion PM): Hi all. we want to make sure this POC gives us clear go/no-go metrics.
[00:16] Priya (Redwood SE): great. agenda — confirm success criteria, go over current stack and traffic, walk model shortlist and tradeoffs, and agree benchmarks + timeline. sound good?
[00:25] Aiko (Synthion ML Eng): yep. quick note: our workload is multilingual customer support — en/es/fr/ja primarily, occasional de/it. mostly short messages 10-40 tokens per user turn; long threads can reach up to ~800 tokens total.
[00:38] Jordan: perfect. can you share concurrent session numbers?
[00:41] Oliver (Infra): right now peak concurrent customer chat sessions are ~1200, average concurrent during business hours ~450. monthly token usage ~180M tokens currently (including historical logs).
[00:53] Priya: good, that gives us an idea for throughput. for the POC we usually run a scaled benchmark that represents 10% of your peak to keep cost reasonable but still surface latency/cost behavior.
[01:04] Carlos: makes sense. main success criteria for us: 1) 95th percentile latency under 800ms for single-turn summarization, 2) extractive classification F1 > 0.85 on our labeled set, 3) hallucination rate under 2% on verification prompts, and 4) cost per 1M tokens under $X (we'll provide target).
[01:22] Jordan: good, we can map those to tests. any compliance/security must-haves?
[01:26] Maya: SOC2 is required. also we need audit logs and SSO, and a preference for VPC/private deployment for production. POC can be hosted but must pass data residency checks — European traffic needs to remain in eu region for those customers.
[01:41] Priya: okay we can accommodate. for the POC we'll run on Redwood hosted in eu-west for eu testcases and us-west for us. for production you can evaluate Dedicated or Private later.
[01:52] Aiko: about models — Carlos, we care about multilingual quality first, then cost. we also have domain specific phrases (support/terms) so instruction tuning and few-shot prompts help.
[02:03] Liam (Redwood): good signal. here's the shortlist we suggest for the POC: Llama 3 7B instruct (fast, smaller), Llama 3 13B (higher quality), Mistral-Instruct (strong on instruction following and multilingual), Falcon 40B (very capable but heavier), and an OpenLLaMA 13B variant we can finetune lightly. each has tradeoffs.
[02:26] Carlos: can you run through the expected latency/cost profile for those?
[02:29] Priya: rough numbers — Llama 3 7B on int8: p95 latency ~250-400ms for 1-2 tokens per step with our runtime, cost low. Llama 3 13B int8: p95 ~400-700ms, better quality. Mistral-Instruct 7B/8B variants often match 13B quality on instruction tasks and are good for multilingual. Falcon 40B is slower p95 ~1-1.6s unless you run on Dedicated with larger batch optimizations; cost significantly higher but top-tier on long form QA/knowledge.
[03:08] Maya: we're sensitive to latency — 800ms p95 is our threshold. that makes Falcon 40B risky unless you do Dedicated.
[03:14] Oliver: do you have numbers for quantized 4-bit? we've seen drift issues with 4-bit on some models.
[03:19] Priya: yes, quant-4 can reduce memory and cost by ~2x compared to int8 but sometimes increases hallucination and quality variance. we recommend int8 for the POC to reduce variables. if you want to push cost we can run a 4-bit experiment as a later step.
[03:34] Aiko: about multilingual — do these models natively support ja/es/fr or do we need translation layer?
[03:39] Liam: Mistral and Llama family have decent multilingual, Llama 3 trained more heavily on English but still ok, Mistral tends to be better out-of-the-box for non-English instruction. we recommend having testsets in each language and measuring per-locale F1.
[03:53] Carlos: ok. timeline — what does a standard 4-week POC look like?
[03:56] Jordan: typical plan: Week 0 (kickoff + data prep), Week 1 (baseline benchmarks across models on a representative prompt set), Week 2 (tune prompts and runtime config, run larger throughput tests), Week 3 (multilingual and hallucination/regression tests, debug), Week 4 (wrap, review, exec summary and recommended path for prod). we can compress to 3 weeks if you provide labeled test sets and infra support.
[04:21] Maya: we can commit to providing labeled set for classification and a 200-sample multilingual hallucination checklist within 3 business days post-kickoff.
[04:30] Carlos: who owns running the actual benchmark infra? Redwood or Synthion?
[04:33] Priya: for hosted POC Redwood will run the benchmarks and provide results + raw outputs; we'll need a secure ingest of your prompts and labels. if you prefer to run locally on Dedicated we can provide config + runner.
[04:45] Oliver: data security — what's the retention policy for POC logs?
[04:48] Jordan: by default POC logs are retained 30 days. we can disable retention or set to enterprise retention and configure audit export.
[04:56] Aiko: prompt engineering — what's expected? do you help craft few-shot templates for multilingual?
[04:59] Priya: yes, we include prompt templates and initial tuning. we'll try a few canonical few-shot designs per language and measure sensitivity.
[05:08] Carlos: okay. benchmarks — can you outline the scoring metrics you'll return?
[05:11] Liam: we'll return: latency p50/p95, tokens/sec (throughput), classification precision/recall/F1 per locale, extractive accuracy, hallucination rate (binary verified vs hallucinated), and cost per 1M tokens. each metric will be per-model and per-quantization variant tested.
[05:25] Maya: do you simulate our concurrency with continuous batching to approximate real-world latency?
[05:29] Priya: yes, we'll replay traffic patterns you provide to simulate our runtime batching. we'll surface expected change if you shift to Dedicated or increase batch windows.
[05:38] Carlos: about hallucination — our definition is any confident assertion of incorrect facts about policy or account info. can you flag confidence/likelihood scores?
[05:46] Liam: we can add a hallucination check pass where we run verification prompts and score model responses. we'll surface a confidence score derived from heuristics and answer verification.
[05:55] Aiko: any recommended baseline prompts? we have some but open to Redwood examples.
[05:59] Priya: we'll share a starter prompt pack (few-shot templates in en/es/fr/ja) and you can extend.
[06:05] Jordan: competitors — any firms you're comparing to?
[06:07] Carlos: yeah, we're also evaluating Anthropic and OpenAI plus an in-house smaller LLM.
[06:12] Jordan: good to know. we'll make sure the POC benchmarks address those axes where possible.
[06:16] Maya: deployment note — after POC if we go prod we'll need SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, and KMS integration for key management.
[06:25] Jordan: noted — we support SAML and KMS integrations on Private/Dedicated. for Hosted we offer Bring-Your-Own-Key with HSM options.
[06:34] Oliver: Region routing — can we ensure eu traffic stays in eu?
[06:37] Priya: yes, routing policy can pin requests by region and we can run EU tests in eu-west only for the POC.
[06:44] Carlos: are there any gotchas in scoring multilingual quality given tokenization differences?
[06:49] Liam: yeah tokenization and subword splits can bias per-token latency and cost. we'll normalize metrics by characters and provide both token-normalized and per-request cost.
[06:58] Aiko: about fine-tuning — would you recommend light finetune on our support transcripts?
[07:02] Priya: for this POC we prefer instruction-tuning via few-shot and prompt tuning. full fine-tune adds time and data governance complexity. we can discuss a targeted LoRA/adapter step after you validate model family.
[07:15] Maya: any initial recommendation for the top 2 models to test first?
[07:18] Jordan: based on your latency threshold and multilingual need: Mistral-Instruct (or Mistral 7B instruct variant) and Llama 3 13B (int8) as primary; add Llama 3 7B as a low-cost baseline. Falcon 40B only if you want to test edge quality under Dedicated.
[07:35] Carlos: sounds good. can you put together an initial benchmark plan and estimated cost for the POC?
[07:39] Jordan: yes — we'll email a proposal with the test matrix: 3 models x 2 quant variants x 4 locales x throughput tests, plus per-model scoring. estimate included.
[07:49] Maya: is there a published performance profile we can reference?
[07:52] Priya: yes we'll share our model perf spreadsheet (redwood-perf-v1) and a sample runner script.
[07:58] Carlos: ok next steps and owners?
[08:01] Jordan: quick recap then.
[08:03] Jordan: Next steps: Redwood to share benchmark plan and cost estimate, Redwood to share starter prompts and security docs, Synthion to provide labeled classification set and hallucination checklist, schedule kickoff and provide region preference.
[08:17] Maya: timeline — we can start next Monday.
[08:19] Jordan: great, we'll target a kickoff on 2027-03-15 then.
[08:23] Aiko: any expected blockers?
[08:25] Liam: only blocker is data access/ingest. if you can share sanitized prompts and labels quickly we can proceed.
[08:33] Oliver: i'll coordinate with Priya on SSO and retention settings.
[08:37] Jordan: perfect. action items and owners are in the notes.
[08:41] Maya: thanks everyone.
[08:43] Jordan: thanks — we'll follow up with docs and the proposal.
[08:47] [end of recording]

Note: transcript contains occasional transcription noise and colloquial speech; speaker turns approximate and timestamps are periodic markers rather than exact token timings.
